title: Happens-before relationship: all rules, why threads read stale values without it
keyPoints: Happens-before is the JMM's visibility guarantee: if action A happens-before action B, then all writes performed by A are visible to B.
Without happens-before, a thread can read stale values forever because the JIT may cache variables in CPU registers.
Seven rules: program order, monitor unlock-then-lock, volatile write-then-read, Thread.start(), Thread.join(), constructor final field freeze, and transitivity.
Transitivity is the most powerful rule: a volatile write makes ALL prior non-volatile writes visible to a thread that reads the volatile.
The volatile flag pattern exploits transitivity: set data fields, then set volatile flag; reader checks volatile flag, then reads data fields safely.
Thread.start() establishes happens-before between the caller and the new thread body, so all writes before start() are visible to the new thread.
Thread.join() establishes happens-before between the thread body and the caller after join() returns, so all writes in the thread are visible.

s1_definition.oneliner: Happens-before is the JMM's visibility guarantee: if action A happens-before action B, everything A wrote is visible to B, and without this relationship a thread can read stale values forever.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Happens-before** is a formal ordering relationship defined by the Java Memory Model (JSR-133) that guarantees memory visibility between threads.
- **Without it**, the JVM, JIT compiler, and CPU are free to cache variables in registers, reorder instructions, and delay writes to main memory. A reading thread may never see updates made by another thread.
- **Seven rules** establish happens-before edges: (1) program order within a single thread, (2) monitor unlock happens-before subsequent lock on the same monitor, (3) volatile write happens-before subsequent read of the same volatile, (4) Thread.start() happens-before the new thread's first action, (5) a thread's last action happens-before Thread.join() returns, (6) constructor completion happens-before finalizer and final field freeze, (7) transitivity: if A HB B and B HB C, then A HB C.
- **Transitivity** is the most practically important rule: a volatile write makes all prior writes (including non-volatile ones) visible to any thread that subsequently reads the volatile variable.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of a relay race at National Bank of India's annual sports day. Each runner (thread) carries a baton (happens-before edge). When Rajesh passes the baton to Priya at the exchange zone (synchronized unlock/lock or volatile write/read), everything Rajesh wrote in the ledger is guaranteed to be visible to Priya. Without the baton pass, Priya might be reading her own copy of the ledger that was never updated. The baton is the happens-before edge that ensures one runner's work is visible to the next.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Happens-Before Rules Summary
  ════════════════════════════

  Rule 2: Monitor (synchronized)
  Thread-1:  write(data)  →  UNLOCK(lock)
                                  │ HB edge
  Thread-2:                  LOCK(lock)  →  read(data) ← sees write

  Rule 3: Volatile
  Thread-1:  write(data)  →  volatile write(flag)
                                  │ HB edge
  Thread-2:               volatile read(flag)  →  read(data) ← sees write

  Rule 7: Transitivity
  A ──HB──→ B ──HB──→ C
  Therefore: A ──HB──→ C

  data=42 ─HB(program order)─→ flag=true ─HB(volatile)─→ if(flag)
  Therefore: data=42 ─HB(transitivity)─→ if(flag) → read(data)=42
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Happens-before is the JMM's visibility guarantee. If action A happens-before action B, all writes performed by A are visible to B. Without happens-before, a thread can read stale values forever because the JIT may cache variables in CPU registers and never read main memory again. Seven rules establish happens-before edges: program order, monitor unlock/lock, volatile write/read, Thread.start(), Thread.join(), final field freeze, and transitivity.

Transitivity is the most practically important rule. The volatile flag pattern exploits it: write non-volatile data fields, then write a volatile flag. A reader that sees the volatile write also sees all prior non-volatile writes through transitivity. This is how safe publication works without synchronizing every field individually.

At National Bank of India, a configuration reload flag was implemented without volatile. Worker threads cached the flag in a CPU register and never saw the update, causing them to use the old interest rate indefinitely. Adding volatile to the flag established the happens-before edge, and through transitivity, all configuration values became immediately visible to worker threads.

Remember one sentence: happens-before guarantees that one thread's writes are visible to another, and without it the JVM is free to show stale values forever.
